task.description: RE-VALIDATION after rework: ELIXIR-DEV fixed validate_metadata/1's raise-on-malformed-input bug (leading is_map/1 guard + non-string-key guard) and, on its own initiative during the audit, also fixed a second related crash (fetch_event_type/1 -- a nil/atom/integer event_type previously crashed inside Registry.get_type/2's Ecto query before any typed error). Re-run the full INV-1..INV-8 gate fresh -- do not just re-check INV-8, confirm INV-1/INV-7 still hold against the new diff too (fetch_event_type/1 is new code you haven't reviewed yet). Run the scope test and full INV-1..INV-8 gate against branch feature/WF02-REQ025-20260817's diff. This IS a tenant-data path: append/2 writes tenant-scoped rows across 5 tables and derives tenant_id internally from the Ecto :prefix rather than a caller-supplied field -- the exact attribution-integrity mechanism the 0003 addendum specifies. Pay particular attention to: (a) INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- confirm tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 cannot be tricked into deriving the wrong tenant, and confirm the :tenant_id_not_accepted rejection actually fires and is tested against a real attempted mismatch, not just asserted in prose; (b) INV-7 (no raw SQL string interpolation of tenant/user input) -- check the FOR UPDATE lock query and any other raw SQL/fragment usage; (c) whether the metadata pre-transaction validation could be bypassed to smuggle oversized/malicious data into a jsonb column.
acceptance_criteria: scope test explicitly run and recorded against the actual diff
every applicable INV-1..INV-8 invariant checked with its How-to-verify procedure and recorded PASS/FAIL
tenant_id derivation mechanism specifically verified against the 0003 addendum's attribution-integrity reasoning, not just assumed correct because the design doc says so

result.summary:
Re-ran the full INV-1..INV-8 gate fresh against `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/event_store.ex lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` (557 + 37 lines, read in full, not just a diff-of-the-fix).

Scope test: append/2 writes tenant-scoped rows across events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, event_payload_store, event_idempotency; tenant_provisioning.ex adds tenant_id_for_schema_name/1. IN SCOPE.

INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS (re-confirmed, including the new code). (a) Every Repo/Multi call site in event_store.ex still passes `prefix: schema_name` -- re-read all call sites (active_instance_guard, assign_sequence's insert+FOR UPDATE read+update_all, claim_idempotency's insert+get+get_by, insert_event, store_oversized_payload, update_projection); unchanged from the prior pass. (b) `reject_tenant_id/1` still rejects both atom and string `:tenant_id`/`"tenant_id"` keys with `{:error, :tenant_id_not_accepted}` before anything else runs -- confirmed by reading the function body, and empirically re-confirmed no crash/bypass exists (see INV-8 test harness below; the rejection path was not touched by this rework). (c) `tenant_id_for_schema_name/1` (tenant_provisioning.ex) is unchanged in its core regex/UUID-cast logic from the prior PASS; the only addition since is a second function clause `def tenant_id_for_schema_name(_schema_name), do: {:error, :invalid_schema_name}` for non-binary input (the first clause is guarded `when is_binary(schema_name)`) -- this is new code, reviewed directly: it cannot derive a *wrong* tenant (it never partially matches; any non-binary input falls straight to `:invalid_schema_name`, same terminal error as a malformed binary), and empirically verified via scratch/verify_inv8_req025.exs against prefix values nil, an atom, an integer, an unrelated string, and a SQL-metacharacter-laden string (`"tenant_'; DROP TABLE events; --"`) -- all five returned `{:error, :invalid_schema_name}`, none crashed, none produced a wrong tenant_id or reached SQL. `fetch_event_type/1`'s new guard does not touch tenant derivation at all (it runs after tenant_id is already resolved) so it has no bearing on (a)/(b)/(c) beyond what's covered under INV-8 below.

INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE, unchanged (no API/response-shaping code, no scripting sandbox, no lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4/S5 not started).

INV-4 (secrets) -- NOT-APPLICABLE to this diff's content; re-ran both required greps project-wide, no new hits attributable to this diff.

INV-6 -- APPLIES, satisfied by this handoff's explicit per-invariant statement.

INV-7 (no raw SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS, re-confirmed. `grep -n "Repo\.query\|fragment(" lib/letflow/event_store.ex lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` -- zero hits in event_store.ex; `lock_and_increment_sequence/3`'s FOR-UPDATE read uses Ecto's `lock("FOR UPDATE")` composed over `where([s], s.instance_id == ^instance_id)`, a pinned bind param, not a string -- unchanged from prior pass, re-read directly. tenant_provisioning.ex's two pre-existing `Repo.query!` calls (advisory lock, `CREATE SCHEMA`) are untouched by this diff's +37 lines (confirmed against the diff); the new `tenant_id_for_schema_name/1` performs zero SQL -- it is pure string/regex/`Ecto.UUID.cast` logic, no `Repo` call at all, so it cannot be an injection vector regardless of input (empirically confirmed above: even a SQL-metacharacter payload as the `prefix` string never reaches a query, it's rejected by the regex before any DB interaction).

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, FAIL. The two previously-identified crashes are genuinely fixed: `validate_metadata/1` now has a leading `when not is_map(metadata)` clause returning `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}`, and a non-string-key check inside the `cond`; `fetch_event_type/1` now requires `is_binary(event_type) and byte_size(event_type) > 0` before anything reaches `Registry.get_type/2`'s Ecto query. Verified empirically (scratch/verify_inv8_req025.exs, run via `mix run` against the real compiled app, not extracted/reimplemented logic this time): all 8 malformed `event_type` shapes (nil, atom, integer, list, map, empty string, float, boolean) now return `{:error, :missing_event_type}` cleanly, and the four previously-crashing metadata shapes (empty string, integer, atom-keyed map, list-of-non-tuples) now return typed errors. However, a new realistic crash was found that the rework's fix does not cover: **any struct value passed as `attrs[:metadata]` still crashes**, because `is_map/1` returns `true` for structs (a struct is a map with a `:__struct__` key), so `validate_metadata/1`'s leading `not is_map(metadata)` guard does not exclude them, and structs do not reliably support `Enum.find_value/3`'s `{key, value}`-tuple iteration the way plain maps do. Confirmed for three independent struct types, each with a different crash signature: `DateTime.utc_now()` and `URI.parse("https://example.com")` both raise `Protocol.UndefinedError` (`protocol Enumerable not implemented for type DateTime/URI (a struct)`) because those structs don't implement `Enumerable` at all; `MapSet.new([1,2,3])` and `1..5` (a `Range` struct) both *do* implement `Enumerable` but iterate as bare elements rather than `{key, value}` pairs, so they instead raise `FunctionClauseError` inside `validate_metadata/1`'s own anonymous `fn {key, value} -> ... end`. This is the same class of defect the rework was supposed to close (a `with`-chain function returning a raised exception instead of the `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, _}}` its call site in `append/2` expects, on data that is caller/tenant-controlled per this module's own moduledoc), just a shape the fix's `is_map/1` check didn't anticipate. `append/2`'s own `@spec` still promises `{:ok, append_result()} | append_error()` and a raised exception is neither.

Regarding the handoff's specific check (c) (could metadata validation be bypassed to smuggle oversized/malicious data into jsonb): still no -- for any input that survives validation without crashing (plain maps with string keys/values), the entry-count/key-length/value-length checks are sound and unbypassable, unchanged from the prior pass. The struct-shaped crash is an availability/robustness defect (INV-8), not a data-integrity bypass (INV-1) or injection (INV-7) -- consistent with the prior pass's finding that the *original* validate_metadata bug was also INV-8-only, not INV-1/INV-7.

Single FAIL on an applicable invariant (INV-8) terminates validation per this role's procedure -- overall result FAIL. INV-1 and INV-7 both re-confirmed PASS against the full current diff, including the code that was new to this reviewer (fetch_event_type/1, tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's new catch-all clause).
issues: INV-8 FAIL: lib/letflow/event_store.ex validate_metadata/1 (private fn) still raises on struct-shaped attrs[:metadata] -- is_map/1 is true for structs, so the rework's leading `when not is_map(metadata)` guard does not exclude them. Reproduced for 4 distinct struct types via scratch/verify_inv8_req025.exs (run with `mix run`, real compiled app, no DB needed since this path is pure): DateTime.utc_now() and URI.parse(...) raise Protocol.UndefinedError ('protocol Enumerable not implemented for type ... (a struct)'); MapSet.new([1,2,3]) and 1..5 (a Range struct) raise FunctionClauseError inside validate_metadata/1's own `fn {key, value} -> ... end` because they iterate as bare elements, not {key, value} pairs. Fix: exclude structs explicitly, e.g. a leading clause `defp validate_metadata(metadata) when is_struct(metadata), do: {:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}` ahead of (or combined with, via `not is_map(metadata) or is_struct(metadata)`) the existing `not is_map(metadata)` clause -- do not rely on `is_map/1` alone to mean 'plain map' anywhere malformed tenant-controlled input can reach it. Route to ELIXIR-DEV for the fix; re-submit to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) once corrected, per WF-02's rework loop. Verification harness left at scratch/verify_inv8_req025.exs (git-ignored, not committed) for the next rework pass to reuse/extend.
result.next_action: Rework ELIXIR-DEV -- fix INV-8 violation in validate_metadata/1 (event_store.ex): struct-shaped metadata (DateTime, URI, MapSet, Range, or any other struct) still crashes instead of returning a typed error. Re-submit to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) once corrected.
